metadata.title: A Resolvent Framework for Global and Local Nonlinear Semigroups

nodes.statement: A \emph{query} is a measurable space representing the possible outcomes of asking a single question or making a single observation.
nodes.section: 2.1 Core Definitions
nodes.label: def:query

nodes.statement: A \emph{refinement} between queries is a measurable function showing how outcomes of one query determine outcomes of another.
nodes.section: 2.1 Core Definitions
nodes.label: def:refine

nodes.statement: A \emph{query system} is a preordered family of queries with coherent refinement maps. It consists of: \begin{itemize} \item An index type $\iota$ \item A family of queries $q : \iota \to \text{Query}$ \item A preorder relation $\le$ on indices \item Refinement maps $\pi : \forall \{i\ j\}, i \le j \to \text{Refine}(q_i, q_j)$ \end{itemize} subject to functoriality conditions.
nodes.section: 2.1 Core Definitions
nodes.label: def:query-system

nodes.statement: The \emph{projective limit} $\Omega$ is the space of coherent families of query outcomes. An element $\omega : \Omega$ assigns to each query $i$ an outcome $\omega(i)$, subject to the coherence condition: whenever $i \le j$, we have $\omega(j) = \pi_{ij}(\omega(i))$.
nodes.section: 2.1 Core Definitions
nodes.label: def:omega

nodes.statement: A \emph{cylinder set} $\text{Cyl}(i, A)$ is the set of realizations where query $i$ yields an outcome in $A$. These generate the observable $\sigma$-algebra.
nodes.section: 2.1 Core Definitions
nodes.label: def:cylinder

nodes.statement:
A family $
u$ of measures on query outcomes is \emph{compatible} if the measures commute with refinement maps: whenever $i \le j$, the pushforward of $
u_i$ along $\pi_{ij}$ equals $
u_j$.
nodes.section: 2.1 Core Definitions
nodes.label: def:compatible-marginals

nodes.name: Upper-directed
nodes.statement: A query system is \emph{upper-directed} if any two queries have a common refinement: $\forall i\,j, \exists k, i \le k \land j \le k$.
nodes.section: 2.1 Core Definitions
nodes.label: def:upper-directed

nodes.name: Sequentially upper-directed
nodes.statement: Every \emph{sequence} of queries has a common refinement: $\forall u : \mathbb{N} \to \iota, \exists k, \forall n, u_n \le k$. Strictly stronger than upper-directedness, which bounds pairs. It says the completed query $\bigvee_n Q_n$ is itself a query.
nodes.section: 2.1 Core Definitions
nodes.label: def:seq-upper-directed

nodes.name: Surjective evaluations
nodes.statement: Every evaluation $\mathrm{eval}_i : \Omega \to \mathrm{Outcome}_i$ is surjective: each local outcome extends to a coherent global realization. It gives $\mathrm{Cyl}_k E_1 = \mathrm{Cyl}_k E_2 \Rightarrow E_1 = E_2$.
nodes.section: 2.1 Core Definitions
nodes.label: def:eval-surjective

nodes.statement: Under upper-directedness, the cylinder family forms a $\pi$-system.
nodes.section: 2.2 Main Results
nodes.label: lem:pi-system

nodes.statement: Upper-directedness gives a common refinement of any two cylinder-generating queries; intersect the pulled-back events there.
nodes.section: 2.2 Main Results

nodes.name: Observational Determination
nodes.statement: Two (finite) measures on the projective limit $\Omega$ are equal if and only if they have equal marginals on all queries, i.e.\ equal pushforwards along every $\mathrm{eval}_i$. No compatibility hypothesis is consumed.
nodes.section: 2.2 Main Results
nodes.label: thm:observational-determination

nodes.statement: Apply the $\pi$-$\lambda$ theorem to the cylinder $\sigma$-algebra. The cylinders form a $\pi$-system by \ref{lem:pi-system}, and the hypothesis gives agreement on all cylinders.
nodes.section: 2.2 Main Results

nodes.name: Premeasure Well-Definedness
nodes.statement: The premeasure defined on finite cylinders is well-defined: it doesn't depend on the choice of common \emph{upper} bound (refinement level) used in its definition.
nodes.section: 2.2 Main Results
nodes.label: lem:premu-well-defined

nodes.statement: Given two upper bounds, use upper-directedness to find a common refinement of both. Show the measure values agree using compatibility and proof irrelevance for the transitivity witnesses.
nodes.section: 2.2 Main Results

nodes.name: Stone space of a query system
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{St}(S)$ is the space of ultrafilters on $\Omega$, i.e. the Stone--\v{C}ech compactification of $\Omega$ regarded as a discrete set. It is compact, Hausdorff and totally disconnected.
nodes.section: 3.1 Charges, collective exhaustion, and the Stone space
nodes.label: def:stone-space

nodes.name: Cylinder clopens
nodes.statement: The sets $\{u : E \in u\}$ for $E$ a cylinder event. These are clopen, form a set semiring, and generate the $\sigma$-algebra used on $\mathrm{St}(S)$.
nodes.section: 3.1 Charges, collective exhaustion, and the Stone space
nodes.label: def:stone-clopens

nodes.name: Normalized compatible contents
nodes.statement: A family $\nu_i$ of finitely additive contents on the outcome spaces, compatible under refinement, each of total mass $1$. Finitely additive only.
nodes.section: 3.1 Charges, collective exhaustion, and the Stone space
nodes.label: def:ncc

nodes.name: Collective exhaustion
nodes.statement: For every index $i$ and every decreasing sequence of measurable events shrinking to $\emptyset$, some finer level $j \geq i$ witnesses convergence: the charge of the pulled-back sequence at $j$ tends to $0$. Index-layer conditions do not suffice (\texttt{counterexampleQS\_no\_finitary\_condition}).
nodes.section: 3.1 Charges, collective exhaustion, and the Stone space
nodes.label: def:collectively-exhaustive

nodes.name: Collective exhaustion is per-level $\sigma$-additivity
nodes.statement: $\nu$ is collectively exhaustive if and only if every $\nu_i$ is continuous at $\emptyset$, i.e. $\sigma$-additive.
nodes.section: 3.1 Charges, collective exhaustion, and the Stone space
nodes.label: lem:ce-levelwise

nodes.statement: Compatibility gives $\nu_i(A) = \nu_j(\pi^{-1}A)$ outright, so the quantity tested at the finer level $j$ is equal to the one at $i$ and the existential in \ref{def:collectively-exhaustive} is cosmetic.
nodes.section: 3.1 Charges, collective exhaustion, and the Stone space

nodes.name: SP1
nodes.statement: Collective exhaustion holds if and only if every level's content extends to a genuine measure on that level's outcome space.
nodes.section: 3.1 Charges, collective exhaustion, and the Stone space
nodes.label: thm:sp1-iff

nodes.statement: By \ref{lem:ce-levelwise} collective exhaustion is continuity at $\emptyset$ of each $\nu_i$, which for a content on a $\sigma$-algebra is countable additivity.
nodes.section: 3.1 Charges, collective exhaustion, and the Stone space

nodes.name: Observational extension, sequential form
nodes.statement: If $S$ is \emph{sequentially} upper-directed with surjective evaluations and $\nu_i$ is a compatible family of probability \emph{measures}, then there is a unique probability measure $P$ on $\Omega$ with $\mathrm{map}(\mathrm{eval}_i)\,P = \nu_i$ for every $i$.
nodes.section: 3.2 The extension theorem
nodes.label: thm:observational-extension-seq

nodes.statement: Carath\'eodory on the cylinder semiring. Build the cylinder content --- its value on a cylinder is \texttt{pre}$\mu$ at a singleton presentation, so \ref{lem:premu-well-defined} is what makes the content well defined --- prove $\sigma$-subadditivity (\ref{lem:cylgen-sigma-subadd}), extend, recover marginals; uniqueness is \ref{thm:observational-determination}.
nodes.section: 3.2 The extension theorem

nodes.name: $\sigma$-subadditivity from a common upper bound
nodes.statement: Under sequential upper-directedness (with surjective evaluations and compatible marginal measures) the cylinder content is $\sigma$-subadditive.
nodes.section: 3.2 The extension theorem
nodes.label: lem:cylgen-sigma-subadd

nodes.statement: Sequentiality is used exactly once: given a countable cover, it produces a \emph{single} index $m$ above every index appearing in it, after which $\sigma$-subadditivity of the one measure $\nu_m$ finishes the argument. Ordinary upper-directedness bounds \emph{pairs} of indices, not countable families, so no single $\nu_m$ dominates a countable cover; with ordinary upper-directedness plus collective exhaustion in place of sequentiality this lemma is \textbf{false}, by the Andersen--Jessen system of \S\ref{sec:sequentiality}.
nodes.section: 3.2 The extension theorem

nodes.name: Observational extension from charges
nodes.statement: For a \emph{sequentially} upper-directed query system with surjective evaluations and a collectively exhaustive normalized compatible family $\nu$ of finitely additive charges, there is a unique probability measure $\mu$ on $\Omega$ with $\mu(\mathrm{Cyl}_i A) = \nu_i(A)$ for every query $i$ and measurable $A$.
nodes.section: 3.2 The extension theorem
nodes.label: thm:stone-observational-extension

nodes.statement: \ref{thm:sp1-iff} converts collective exhaustion into a genuine measure at each level; compatibility transfers because each $\mu_i$ agrees with $\nu_i$ on every measurable set; and \ref{thm:observational-extension-seq} finishes on $\Omega$, its uniqueness clause included.
nodes.section: 3.2 The extension theorem

nodes.name: The Stone measure exists and extends the content
nodes.statement: There is a probability measure $\hat P$ on $\mathrm{St}(S)$ with $\hat P(E) = m(E)$ for every cylinder clopen $E$, where $m$ is the additive content transferred from $\nu$ along the Stone embedding. No collective exhaustion and no directedness beyond upper is used.
nodes.section: 3.4 The finitely additive theorem on the Stone space
nodes.label: thm:stone-measure-exists

nodes.statement: Transfer $\nu$ to an additive content on the cylinder clopens; prove $\sigma$-subadditivity using compactness of the Stone space (every countable cover of a clopen has a finite subcover); apply Carath\'eodory.
nodes.section: 3.4 The finitely additive theorem on the Stone space

nodes.name: Escaping tower
nodes.statement: A decreasing sequence of cylinder events, each of full charge, with empty intersection.
nodes.section: 3.5 The obstruction, formalized
nodes.label: def:escaping-tower

nodes.name: No extension over an escaping tower
nodes.statement: A query system carrying an escaping tower admits no extension of its charges to a probability measure on $\Omega$. No hypotheses on $S$ are used --- no directedness, no surjectivity, no collective exhaustion.
nodes.section: 3.5 The obstruction, formalized
nodes.label: thm:no-extension-tower

nodes.statement: The tower's cylinders are an antitone measurable sequence with empty intersection and every stage of mass $1$, which is exactly what \ref{lem:cont-above} forbids.
nodes.section: 3.5 The obstruction, formalized

nodes.name: The obstruction is not vacuous
nodes.statement: The finite--cofinite query system carries an escaping tower: with $E_n = \mathbb{Q} \setminus \{q_0,\dots,q_n\}$, each $E_n$ is cofinite hence in the hyperfilter hence of content $1$, while $\bigcap_n E_n = \emptyset$.
nodes.section: 3.5 The obstruction, formalized
nodes.label: thm:tower-inhabited

nodes.statement: Direct.
nodes.section: 3.5 The obstruction, formalized

nodes.name: The finite--cofinite system admits no extension
nodes.statement: The finite--cofinite query system admits no extension of its charges to a probability measure on $\Omega$. It fails collective exhaustion (\texttt{counterexampleNCC\_not\_collectivelyExhaustive}), so it does not refute the plain-upper-directedness extension statement of \S\ref{sec:sequentiality}.
nodes.section: 3.5 The obstruction, formalized
nodes.label: cor:cex-no-extension

nodes.statement: Instantiate \ref{thm:no-extension-tower} at the finite--cofinite escaping tower of \ref{thm:tower-inhabited}.
nodes.section: 3.5 The obstruction, formalized

nodes.name: The group
nodes.statement: $A = \mathbb{Z} + \alpha\mathbb{Z}$ for $\alpha$ irrational (as a set, and as the additive subgroup \texttt{Afull} of $\mathbb{R}$). Countable.
nodes.section: 4 Andersen--Jessen: the thick tower and the diagonal layer
nodes.label: def:aj-A

nodes.name: Density
nodes.statement: $A$ is dense in $\mathbb{R}$.
nodes.section: 4 Andersen--Jessen: the thick tower and the diagonal layer
nodes.label: lem:aj-dense

nodes.statement: $2\mathbb{Z}+\alpha\mathbb{Z}$ is a subgroup, so by \texttt{AddSubgroup.dense\_or\_cyclic} it is dense or cyclic; a generator $g$ would give $2 = pg$ and $\alpha = qg$, making $\alpha = 2q/p$ rational. Density of $A$ follows by monotonicity.
nodes.section: 4 Andersen--Jessen: the thick tower and the diagonal layer

nodes.name: The transversal
nodes.statement: $V$, a set of coset representatives for $\mathbb{R}/A$: two representatives congruent mod $A$ are equal.
nodes.section: 4 Andersen--Jessen: the thick tower and the diagonal layer
nodes.label: lem:aj-V

nodes.statement: \texttt{Quotient.out} on $\mathbb{R} \mathbin{/} A$.
nodes.section: 4 Andersen--Jessen: the thick tower and the diagonal layer

nodes.name: Finiteness beats parity
nodes.statement: For FINITE $F \subseteq A$, the set $V + F$ contains no measurable set of positive measure.
nodes.section: 4 Andersen--Jessen: the thick tower and the diagonal layer
nodes.label: thm:aj-finite

nodes.statement: If it did, Steinhaus (\texttt{Measure.sub\_mem\_nhds\_zero\_of\_addHaar\_pos}) puts a neighbourhood of $0$ inside $F' - F'$. $F - F$ is finite while $A$ is dense, so some element of $A$ lies in that neighbourhood and outside $F - F$; the transversal then forces it into $F - F$ after all.
nodes.section: 4 Andersen--Jessen: the thick tower and the diagonal layer

nodes.name: The thick tower
nodes.statement: With $A$ enumerated, set $X_k = V + \{a_j : j \geq k\}$. Then $X_k$ is decreasing (\texttt{X\_antitone}), $\bigcap_k X_k = \emptyset$ (\texttt{X\_iInter}), and every $X_k$ is thick: any measurable set disjoint from it is null.
nodes.section: 4 Andersen--Jessen: the thick tower and the diagonal layer
nodes.label: thm:aj-tower

nodes.statement: $X_k^c = V + \{a_0,\dots,a_{k-1}\}$, a finite subset of $A$, so \ref{thm:aj-finite} applies at every $k$. The empty intersection needs only the enumeration covering $A$ and the transversal property (\ref{lem:aj-V}): each real decomposes as $v + a$ with $v$ forced, and $a$ eventually falls out of every tail.
nodes.section: 4 Andersen--Jessen: the thick tower and the diagonal layer

nodes.name: Thickness, relative to a base measure
nodes.statement: $X$ is \emph{thick for} $\mu$ when every measurable set disjoint from $X$ is $\mu$-null. The base is arbitrary rather than Lebesgue because the marginals need mass $1$ and $\lambda(\mathbb{R}) = \infty$, while $X_k \cap [0,1]$ is not thick in $\mathbb{R}$.
nodes.section: 4.1 The trace measure, and the refutation
nodes.label: def:thick-for

nodes.name: The trace measure on a thick set
nodes.statement: For $X$ thick for $\mu$, the traces $\{E \cap X\}$ carry a measure with $\lambda_X(E \cap X) = \mu(E)$ (Border, Prop.~14).
nodes.section: 4.1 The trace measure, and the refutation
nodes.label: thm:trace-measure

nodes.statement: The $\sigma$-algebra is the comap one, but the measure must be built by \texttt{Measure.ofMeasurable}: \texttt{Measure.comap} returns $0$ for a thick set with thick complement. Well-definedness is where thickness is spent --- two measurable sets with the same trace differ by a measurable set disjoint from $X$, hence null --- and $\sigma$-additivity follows because disjoint traces force a.e.-disjoint representatives.
nodes.section: 4.1 The trace measure, and the refutation

nodes.name: Andersen--Jessen admits no extension
nodes.statement: The Andersen--Jessen query system carries compatible $\sigma$-additive probability marginals and admits no extension to a probability measure on $\Omega$.
nodes.section: 4.1 The trace measure, and the refutation
nodes.label: thm:aj-no-extension

nodes.statement: The levels carry trace measures (\ref{thm:trace-measure}) over the restricted base, so each is a probability measure, and they are compatible along the tower's inclusions. Pushing them along the diagonal gives Kolmogorov-consistent marginals; the commutation $\mathrm{bond} \circ \mathrm{diag} = \mathrm{diag} \circ \mathrm{incl}$ is definitional. The diagonal cylinders then form an escaping tower: each carries full mass because the diagonal map lands in the diagonal, and their intersection is empty by \ref{thm:diag-empty}. A coherent family is not a sequence, so it is carried to one by $\mathrm{toSeq}\,\omega : k \mapsto (\omega_k)_k$, reading off the top coordinate at each level. Every entry lies in its own $X_k$ by the subtype alone, while constancy needs both the coherence (to move coordinate $0$ down from level $i$ to level $0$) and the base cylinders (to move it across level $i$ from coordinate $0$ to coordinate $i$). \ref{thm:diag-empty} then supplies the emptiness, against \ref{thm:aj-tower}, and \ref{thm:no-extension-tower} finishes.
nodes.section: 4.1 The trace measure, and the refutation

nodes.name: The hypotheses, discharged
nodes.statement: The Andersen--Jessen system is upper-directed, and every level's evaluation is onto.
nodes.section: 4.1 The trace measure, and the refutation
nodes.label: thm:aj-hypotheses

nodes.statement: $\iota = \mathbb{N}$ under $\leq$, so upper bounds are maxima. For surjectivity, extend a given level-$n$ outcome by an arbitrary choice above $n$; the result is coherent and restricts correctly.
nodes.section: 4.1 The trace measure, and the refutation

nodes.name: The \texttt{UpperDirected} form is false
nodes.statement: There is a query system satisfying \texttt{UpperDirected} and \texttt{EvalSurjective} whose compatible $\sigma$-additive marginals admit no extension.
nodes.section: 4.1 The trace measure, and the refutation
nodes.label: cor:upper-directed-false

nodes.statement: The Andersen--Jessen system, with \ref{thm:aj-hypotheses} supplying the two hypotheses and \ref{thm:aj-no-extension} the failure. At $\iota = \mathbb{N}$ the two hypotheses come apart: every finite set of levels has an upper bound, an unbounded sequence of them does not. Collective exhaustion is not discharged, so the form including that hypothesis is not refuted by this corollary.
nodes.section: 4.1 The trace measure, and the refutation

nodes.name: Diagonal cylinders
nodes.statement: $D_n = \{\omega : \omega_i = \omega_0 \text{ for all } i \leq n\}$ inside $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$ with the product $\sigma$-algebra, and $\Pi'(Y) = \{\omega : \omega_k \in Y_k \text{ for all } k\}$ (\texttt{Pi'}). The cylinders decrease (\texttt{Diag\_antitone}), and a point of $D_n$ is determined on $[0,n]$ by its first coordinate (\texttt{Diag\_eq\_of\_le}).
nodes.section: 4.2 The diagonal layer
nodes.label: def:diag-cylinders

nodes.name: The cylinders shrink to the constants
nodes.statement: $\bigcap_n D_n = \{\omega : \omega_i = \omega_0 \text{ for all } i\}$: the sequences that are constant outright.
nodes.section: 4.2 The diagonal layer
nodes.label: lem:diag-inter

nodes.statement: Both inclusions are immediate from the definition; the forward one reads off the bound $i \leq n$ at $n = i$.
nodes.section: 4.2 The diagonal layer

nodes.name: The diagonal escapes
nodes.statement: If $\bigcap_k Y_k = \emptyset$ then $\Pi'(Y) \cap \bigcap_n D_n = \emptyset$, generically in $Y$.
nodes.section: 4.2 The diagonal layer
nodes.label: thm:diag-empty

nodes.statement: A point of every $D_n$ is constant by \ref{lem:diag-inter}, so its common value $\omega_0$ lies in $Y_k$ for every $k$, i.e.\ in $\bigcap_k Y_k = \emptyset$.
nodes.section: 4.2 The diagonal layer

nodes.name: The cylinders are measurable
nodes.statement: Each $D_n$ is measurable.
nodes.section: 4.2 The diagonal layer
nodes.label: lem:diag-measurable

nodes.statement: Coordinate evaluation is measurable (\texttt{measurable\_coord}), hence so is agreement of two coordinates (\texttt{measurableSet\_eq\_coord}), and $D_n = \bigcap_{i \leq n} \{\omega : \omega_i = \omega_0\}$ is a finite intersection of those.
nodes.section: 4.2 The diagonal layer

nodes.name: Continuity from above, in the form the contradiction uses
nodes.statement: A probability measure cannot give every term of an antitone measurable sequence mass one when the intersection is empty.
nodes.section: 4.2 The diagonal layer
nodes.label: lem:cont-above

nodes.statement: The measures converge to that of the intersection, which is $0$; if every term were $1$ the limit would be both $0$ and $1$.
nodes.section: 4.2 The diagonal layer

nodes.name: Delay query
nodes.statement: Over a sensor alphabet $X$, the observation space is the bi-infinite stream space $\Omega = X^{\mathbb{Z}}$. The query at $(d,\tau)$ reads $d$ samples backwards at lag $\tau$: \[ \mathrm{eval}_{d,\tau}(\omega) = (\omega_0, \omega_{-\tau}, \omega_{-2\tau}, \dots, \omega_{-(d-1)\tau}) \in X^d . \]
nodes.section: 5.1 The delay system
nodes.label: def:delay-query

nodes.name: Delay refinement
nodes.statement: $(d,\tau) \leq (d',\tau')$ when $\tau' \mid \tau$ and $d' > (d-1)(\tau/\tau')$: the finer lag divides the coarser one, and the finer window is long enough to span the coarser one. The refinement map keeps the coordinates at positions $0, \tau/\tau', \dots, (d-1)\tau/\tau'$.
nodes.section: 5.1 The delay system
nodes.label: def:delay-refine

nodes.name: The delay system is a query system
nodes.statement: $(d,\tau) \mapsto$ the delay query, with the refinement above, satisfies the query-system axioms.
nodes.section: 5.1 The delay system
nodes.label: thm:delay-qs

nodes.statement: Reflexivity and transitivity of the order are divisibility and arithmetic; $\pi_{\mathrm{refl}}$ and $\pi_{\mathrm{trans}}$ are index computations on coordinate selections.
nodes.section: 5.1 The delay system

nodes.name: Upper-directed
nodes.statement: Any two delay queries have a common refinement.
nodes.section: 5.1 The delay system
nodes.label: thm:delay-upper

nodes.statement: Take lag $\gcd(\tau,\tau')$ and depth $\max\{(d-1)(\tau/\gcd), (d'-1)(\tau'/\gcd)\} + 1$. The gcd divides both lags, and the depth is chosen to span both windows.
nodes.section: 5.1 The delay system

nodes.name: The delay system is NOT sequentially upper-directed
nodes.statement: There is no single query above the whole sequence $u_n = (n+2,\ 1)$.
nodes.section: 5.2 The gap, exhibited
nodes.label: thm:delay-not-sud

nodes.statement: An upper bound $(d'',\tau'')$ would need $\tau'' \mid 1$, hence $\tau''=1$, and then $(n+2)-1 = n+1 < d''$ for every $n$ --- impossible for a finite $d''$.
nodes.section: 5.2 The gap, exhibited

nodes.name: Bounded fixed-lag subsystem
nodes.statement: Fix a lag $\tau_0$ and a maximum depth $N$; index by $\{d \leq N\}$ with the order $d \leq d'$ and coordinate-truncation refinement.
nodes.section: 5.3 Where the extension theorem does apply
nodes.label: def:delay-fixed-lag

nodes.name: The bounded subsystem is sequentially upper-directed
nodes.statement: $N$ is a universal upper bound.
nodes.section: 5.3 Where the extension theorem does apply
nodes.label: thm:delay-fixed-sud

nodes.statement: Every index is $\leq N$, so the constant family at $N$ bounds any sequence.
nodes.section: 5.3 Where the extension theorem does apply

nodes.name: Extension for bounded fixed-lag delay embeddings
nodes.statement: For fixed $\tau_0$ and $N$, any compatible family of probability marginals on $\{X^d : d \leq N\}$ extends \emph{uniquely} to a probability measure on $\Omega$.
nodes.section: 5.3 Where the extension theorem does apply
nodes.label: thm:delay-extension

nodes.statement: \ref{thm:delay-fixed-sud} supplies sequential upper-directedness and \texttt{evalSurjective} the realizability hypothesis; the extension theorem applies directly.
nodes.section: 5.3 Where the extension theorem does apply

nodes.name: The delay map $\Phi_h$
nodes.statement: $\Phi_h(x) = (h(T^n x))_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$, the forward orbit of $x$ seen through the observable $h$. Paper II indexes on $\mathbb{Z}$; the Lean development indexes on $\mathbb{N}$, which for invertible $T$ generates the same $\sigma$-algebra.
nodes.section: 5.4 Reconstruction, and the join to the query system
nodes.label: def:delay-map

nodes.name: The observable algebra $\mathcal{O}_h$
nodes.statement: The $\sigma$-algebra on the state space generated by a family $f : \mathbb{Z} \to (X \to \mathbb{R})$; $\mathcal{O}_h := \mathrm{observableAlgebra}(n \mapsto h \circ T^{n})$ (\texttt{delayObservableAlgebra}).
nodes.section: 5.4 Reconstruction, and the join to the query system
nodes.label: def:observable-algebra

nodes.name: Pullback identity
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{O}_h = \Phi_h^{-1}(\mathcal{B}(\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}))$.
nodes.section: 5.4 Reconstruction, and the join to the query system
nodes.label: thm:obs-eq-comap

nodes.statement: $(\le)$ each generator $h \circ T^{n}$ is $\pi_n \circ \Phi_h$, so its level sets are pullbacks. $(\ge)$ the product $\sigma$-algebra is generated by the coordinate projections, and $\Phi_h^{-1}(\pi_n^{-1}(E)) = (h \circ T^n)^{-1}(E)$.
nodes.section: 5.4 Reconstruction, and the join to the query system

nodes.name: Density bridge, Paper II Lemma 4.3
nodes.statement: The $m$-simple functions are dense in $L^2(X, m, \mu|_m)$.
nodes.section: 5.4 Reconstruction, and the join to the query system
nodes.label: thm:density-bridge

nodes.statement: \texttt{Lp.simpleFunc.dense}.
nodes.section: 5.4 Reconstruction, and the join to the query system

nodes.name: Reconstruction, Paper II Theorem 4.1
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{O}_h = m_0$ modulo $\mu$ if and only if $\mathrm{lpMeas}\,\mathcal{O}_h$ is dense in $L^2(\mu)$; and by \ref{thm:obs-eq-comap} both are equivalent to $\Phi_h$ being a measure-theoretic embedding.
nodes.section: 5.4 Reconstruction, and the join to the query system
nodes.label: thm:reconstruction

nodes.statement: Closed-plus-dense on the \texttt{lpMeas} subspace, with \ref{thm:density-bridge} supplying density.
nodes.section: 5.4 Reconstruction, and the join to the query system

nodes.name: The observation stream of a state
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{orbitStream}\,h\,T\,x$ is the sensor stream a state emits: at time $t$ it carries $h(T^{(-t)^{+}} x)$, the observation of the state $(-t)$ steps ahead.
nodes.section: 5.4 Reconstruction, and the join to the query system
nodes.label: def:orbit-stream

nodes.name: Sampling the orbit stream is taking delay coordinates
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{delayEval}\,d\,\tau\,(\mathrm{orbitStream}\,h\,T\,x) = (h(T^{k\tau} x))_{k < d}$. At $\tau = 1$ this is $\Phi_h$ truncated to its first $d$ coordinates (\texttt{delayEval\_orbitStream\_one}).
nodes.section: 5.4 Reconstruction, and the join to the query system
nodes.label: thm:delay-eval-orbit

nodes.statement: Unfold both sides; the time index $-(k\tau)$ negates to $k\tau$.
nodes.section: 5.4 Reconstruction, and the join to the query system

nodes.name: The bridge: the queries resolve exactly $\mathcal{O}_h$
nodes.statement: Let $\mathrm{delayQueryAlgebra}$ be the $\sigma$-algebra induced on the state space by pulling every delay query's outcome back along \ref{def:orbit-stream}. Then \[ \mathrm{delayQueryAlgebra}\,h\,T = \mathcal{O}_h. \]
nodes.section: 5.4 Reconstruction, and the join to the query system
nodes.label: thm:query-reconstruction-bridge

nodes.statement: $(\le)$ every coordinate of every query is some $h \circ T^{n}$ by \ref{thm:delay-eval-orbit}, so each query map is $\mathcal{O}_h$-measurable and its pullback sits below. $(\ge)$ conversely every generator $h \circ T^{n}$ is a coordinate of the query $(n+1, 1)$; the negative indices of the $\mathbb{Z}$-indexed family collapse to $h$ itself and are covered by $d = 1$. Unit lag alone therefore already generates everything.
nodes.section: 5.4 Reconstruction, and the join to the query system

nodes.name: Lag-$\tau$ data is unit-lag data of the power map
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{delayEval}\,d\,\tau\,(\mathrm{orbitStream}\,h\,T\,x) = (\Phi_h^{T^{\tau}}(x)_k)_{k<d}$.

nodes.statement: A finite $\bot$-closed family of carrier sets.

nodes.label: def:se-block

nodes.name: Intersection-closure
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{InterClosed}(d)$ says $A, A' \in d \Rightarrow A \cap A' \in d$. A Dynkin system with this property is exactly a $\sigma$-algebra, by Dynkin's $\pi$--$\lambda$ theorem.
nodes.section: 6.1 Intersection-closure
nodes.label: def:interclosed

nodes.name: Distributivity is spent here, and only here
nodes.statement: On an intersection-closed carrier a two-valued state is \emph{multiplicative}: if $A$ and $A'$ are true, so is $A \cap A'$.
nodes.section: 6.1 Intersection-closure

nodes.statement: $A = (A \cap A') \sqcup (A \cap A'^{c})$ is a disjoint union inside $d$. Since $A \cap A'^{c} \subseteq A'^{c}$ and $A'$ is true, monotonicity makes $A \cap A'^{c}$ false; additivity on the disjoint pair forces $A \cap A'$ true.

nodes.name: Orthomodular lattice
nodes.statement: A bounded lattice with an order-reversing involution $x \mapsto x^{\perp}$ satisfying $x \wedge x^{\perp} = \bot$, $x \vee x^{\perp} = \top$, and the orthomodular law $x \le y \Rightarrow y = x \vee (y \wedge x^{\perp})$. Distributivity is not assumed; a distributive one is a Boolean algebra.

nodes.label: def:oml

nodes.name: MO$_2$
nodes.statement: The six-element lattice $\{\bot, a, a', b, b', \top\}$ with the four middle elements pairwise incomparable, $a^{\perp} = a'$ and $b^{\perp} = b'$.
nodes.section: 6.2 MO$_2$: the smallest non-distributive witness
nodes.label: def:mo2

nodes.name: MO$_2$ is an orthomodular lattice
nodes.statement: MO$_2$ satisfies every orthomodular lattice axiom.

nodes.statement: All laws are decidable over a six-element type; the instance discharges them by \texttt{decide}.

nodes.name: The non-distributive gap
nodes.statement: In MO$_2$, $a \wedge b = \bot$ while $a \not\le b^{\perp}$.
nodes.section: 6.2 MO$_2$: the smallest non-distributive witness
nodes.label: thm:mo2-gap

nodes.statement: By decision over the finite type.
nodes.section: 6.2 MO$_2$: the smallest non-distributive witness

nodes.name: The four-point carrier
nodes.statement: On $\Omega = \{0,1\}^{2}$ set $A = \{p : p_1 = 1\}$ and $B = \{p : p_2 = 1\}$, and let \[ L \;=\; \{\emptyset, A, A^{c}, \Omega\} \;\cup\; \{\emptyset, B, B^{c}, \Omega\}, \] the horizontal sum of two four-element Boolean blocks glued along $\{\emptyset, \Omega\}$. $L$ is a Dynkin system.
nodes.section: 6.3 MO$_2$ realized: the gap inside a $\sigma$-class
nodes.label: def:concrete-mo2

nodes.statement: Complement-closure is immediate. For countable disjoint unions: two nonempty members of $L$ that are disjoint are complementary, because a member of one block always meets a member of the other --- $A \cap B$, $A \cap B^{c}$, $A^{c} \cap B$, $A^{c} \cap B^{c}$ are each a point. So a disjoint family in $L$ contains at most one nonempty member up to its complement, and its union is $\emptyset$, that member, or $\Omega$.
nodes.section: 6.3 MO$_2$ realized: the gap inside a $\sigma$-class

nodes.name: The carrier is MO$_2$
nodes.statement: The indexing $\bot, a, a', b, b', \top \;\mapsto\; \emptyset, A, A^{c}, B, B^{c}, \Omega$ is a bijection onto $L$; it carries the order of MO$_2$ to inclusion and $(\cdot)^{\perp}$ to set complement.
nodes.section: 6.3 MO$_2$ realized: the gap inside a $\sigma$-class
nodes.label: thm:concrete-mo2-iso

nodes.statement: Inclusion and complement are decidable over four points; injectivity follows from antisymmetry once the order correspondence is known, and surjectivity is the definition of $L$.
nodes.section: 6.3 MO$_2$ realized: the gap inside a $\sigma$-class

nodes.name: Concrete compatibility, and a poor pair
nodes.statement: $A \leftrightarrow B$ (\emph{compatible}) means $A \cap B$ is itself in the carrier. The pair is \emph{poor} when $A \cap B$ is inhabited and yet the only carrier member inside it is $\emptyset$: the lattice meet is $\bot$ while the intersection is not.
nodes.section: 6.3 MO$_2$ realized: the gap inside a $\sigma$-class
nodes.label: def:poor-pair

nodes.name: The four-point carrier has a poor pair
nodes.statement: $A \cap B$ is the single point $(1,1)$, which is not in $L$, and no nonempty member of $L$ fits inside it. So $(A,B)$ is poor, and $A$ and $B$ lie in no common maximal block.
nodes.section: 6.3 MO$_2$ realized: the gap inside a $\sigma$-class
nodes.label: thm:concrete-mo2-poor

nodes.statement: Every nonempty member of $L$ has two points, so a member contained in a subsingleton is empty.
nodes.section: 6.3 MO$_2$ realized: the gap inside a $\sigma$-class

nodes.name: $L$ is not intersection-closed
nodes.statement: $L$ is not intersection-closed.
nodes.section: 6.3 MO$_2$ realized: the gap inside a $\sigma$-class
nodes.label: cor:concrete-mo2-not-interclosed

nodes.statement: $A$ and $B$ lie in $L$ (\ref{thm:concrete-mo2-iso}), so intersection-closure would put $A \cap B$ in $L$ as well. By \ref{thm:concrete-mo2-poor} the only member of $L$ inside $A \cap B$ is $\emptyset$, and $A \cap B$ is inhabited.
nodes.section: 6.3 MO$_2$ realized: the gap inside a $\sigma$-class

nodes.name: Four points are necessary, and $L$ attains the bound
nodes.statement: If $S$ and $T$ lie in a $\sigma$-class and $S \cap T$ does not, then $S \cap T$, $S \setminus T$, $T \setminus S$ and $(S \cup T)^{c}$ are all inhabited, so the carrier has at least four points. Every $\sigma$-class on three or fewer points is therefore intersection-closed, hence a $\sigma$-algebra; and $|\Omega| = 4$, so $L$ realizes the failure on the smallest carrier that admits one.
nodes.section: 6.3 MO$_2$ realized: the gap inside a $\sigma$-class
nodes.label: thm:interclosed-needs-four

nodes.statement: Each cell is forced by a different closure property. $S \cap T = \emptyset$ would put it in the carrier. $S \setminus T = \emptyset$ gives $S \subseteq T$ and $S \cap T = S$; symmetrically $T \setminus S = \emptyset$ gives $S \cap T = T$. And $(S \cup T)^{c} = \emptyset$ makes $S^{c}$ and $T^{c}$ disjoint members, so $S^{c} \cup T^{c}$ lies in the carrier and its complement is $S \cap T$. The four cells are pairwise disjoint, so one point from each gives four distinct points.
nodes.section: 6.3 MO$_2$ realized: the gap inside a $\sigma$-class

nodes.name: Meets exist; the gap is not their absence
nodes.statement: Any two members of $L$ have a greatest member of $L$ below both. In particular $A \wedge B = \emptyset$ while $A \cap B \neq \emptyset$.
nodes.section: 6.3 MO$_2$ realized: the gap inside a $\sigma$-class
nodes.label: thm:concrete-mo2-meets

nodes.statement: Comparable pairs meet at the smaller one. For any other pair the intersection holds at most one point, so by the previous proof the only member below both is $\emptyset$.
nodes.section: 6.3 MO$_2$ realized: the gap inside a $\sigma$-class

nodes.name: Finite truncation $L_2^N$
nodes.statement: $L_2^N := \mathrm{Fin}\,N \to \mathrm{MO}_2$, carrying the product lattice order: $x \le y$ iff $x_i \le y_i$ at every block $i$.
nodes.section: 6.4 The descent ladder: MO$_2$ carried to infinity
nodes.label: def:l2n

nodes.name: Coordinatewise orthocomplement
nodes.section: 6.4 The descent ladder: MO$_2$ carried to infinity
nodes.label: def:pi-ortho

nodes.name: The witness and the family
nodes.statement: $p := b$ on every block, and $a_i := a$ on block $i$, $\bot$ elsewhere (\texttt{QuerySystem.aFam}). The family is orthogonal because its members have disjoint supports.
nodes.section: 6.4 The descent ladder: MO$_2$ carried to infinity
nodes.label: def:descent-witness

nodes.name: $(\star)$ at every finite truncation
nodes.statement: For every $N$ and every block $i < N$, \[ p \sqcap a_i = \bot \quad\text{and}\quad p \not\le a_i^{\perp}. \]
nodes.section: 6.4 The descent ladder: MO$_2$ carried to infinity
nodes.label: thm:star-finite

nodes.statement: Both halves are coordinatewise tests. For the meet: off block $i$ the element $a_i$ is $\bot$, and on block $i$ the meet is $b \sqcap a = \bot$ by \ref{thm:mo2-gap}. For the non-orthogonality: $\le$ on the product is pointwise, so $p \le a_i^{\perp}$ would force $b \le a^{\perp}$ at block $i$, which \ref{thm:mo2-gap} refutes.
nodes.section: 6.4 The descent ladder: MO$_2$ carried to infinity

nodes.name: Navara's $L_2$, blockwise
nodes.statement: The carrier of the $(\beta)$-construction over a countable block index set, with block evaluation $\mathrm{blockVal} : L_2 \to \mathbb{N} \to \mathrm{MO}_2$ and the sublogic-of-product axioms \texttt{le\_iff\_blockwise}, \texttt{blockVal\_ortho}, \texttt{blockVal\_inf}, \texttt{blockVal\_bot}. Cited, not proved.
nodes.section: 6.4 The descent ladder: MO$_2$ carried to infinity
nodes.label: def:navara-l2

nodes.name: $(\star)$ at infinity
nodes.statement: For Navara's witness $p$ and every $n$ in the countable orthogonal family, \[ p \sqcap a_n = \bot \quad\text{and}\quad p \not\le a_n^{\perp}. \]
nodes.section: 6.4 The descent ladder: MO$_2$ carried to infinity
nodes.label: thm:star-infinite

nodes.statement: Verbatim the Rung-2 argument, with \texttt{le\_iff\_blockwise} supplying the coordinatewise order that the product structure gave for free. Antisymmetry of the blockwise order reduces the meet to a blockwise identity; the non-orthogonality is refuted at block $n$.
nodes.section: 6.4 The descent ladder: MO$_2$ carried to infinity

nodes.name: The concrete descent carrier
nodes.statement: On $\Omega = \mathbb{N} \times \{0,1\}^{2}$, the sets every fibre of which lies in the four-point carrier of \ref{def:concrete-mo2}: countably many disjoint copies of MO$_2$.
nodes.section: 6.4 The descent ladder: MO$_2$ carried to infinity
nodes.label: def:concrete-descent

nodes.statement: A Dynkin system. Complement and countable disjoint union are computed fibrewise --- the fibre of a complement is the complement of the fibre, the fibre of a union the union of the fibres, and disjointness passes to fibres --- so each closure property reduces to the same property of \ref{def:concrete-mo2}.
nodes.section: 6.4 The descent ladder: MO$_2$ carried to infinity

nodes.name: $(\star)$ at infinity, on a concrete carrier, with no cited axiom
nodes.statement: Put $p = \{q : q_2 \in B\}$ and $a_n = \{n\} \times A$. Then $\{a_n\}$ is an infinite pairwise-orthogonal family in the carrier, the greatest carrier element below both $p$ and $a_n$ is $\emptyset$, and $p \not\subseteq a_n^{c}$. The carrier is not intersection-closed.
nodes.section: 6.4 The descent ladder: MO$_2$ carried to infinity
nodes.label: thm:concrete-descent

nodes.statement: Orthogonality and distinctness are the block index: $a_n$ and $a_m$ live in different fibres. For the meet, a carrier element below both $p$ and $a_n$ has empty fibre off block $n$, and at block $n$ its fibre sits inside $A \cap B$, a single point, so it is empty by \ref{thm:concrete-mo2-poor}. Non-orthogonality is witnessed at block $n$ by the point $(n, (1,1))$, which lies in $p$ and in $a_n$; that same point is the fibre of $p \cap a_n$, which the carrier does not contain.
nodes.section: 6.4 The descent ladder: MO$_2$ carried to infinity

nodes.name: Products of orthomodular lattices are orthomodular
nodes.statement: If each $\alpha_i$ is an orthomodular lattice then so is $\prod_i \alpha_i$, with lattice operations, bounds and orthocomplement all coordinatewise.
nodes.section: 6.4 The descent ladder: MO$_2$ carried to infinity
nodes.label: thm:prod-oml

nodes.statement: Every law of the class is an equation or an implication between elements, and the product order, lattice and bounded-order structures are pointwise; so each law follows from the same law in each factor, applied at each coordinate.
nodes.section: 6.4 The descent ladder: MO$_2$ carried to infinity

nodes.name: A model of the Rung-3 axioms
nodes.statement: Take $M := \mathbb{N} \to \mathrm{MO}_2$ with all operations coordinatewise, $p := b$ everywhere, $a_n := a$ on block $n$. Then every one of the eleven Rung-3 axioms is a \emph{theorem} about $M$, and $(\star)$ holds in it directly. Hence the axiom set is consistent.
nodes.section: 6.4 The descent ladder: MO$_2$ carried to infinity
nodes.label: thm:descent-consistent

nodes.statement: Each blockwise axiom is the corresponding product lemma. The axiom asserting that $L_2$ is an orthomodular lattice --- without which $\sqcap$, $\le$, $^{\perp}$ and $\bot$ in the other ten are undefined --- is supplied by \ref{thm:prod-oml}, and the model's orthocomplement is definitionally that structure's (\texttt{mOrtho\_eq\_ortho}).
nodes.section: 6.4 The descent ladder: MO$_2$ carried to infinity

nodes.name: The tests localize per block
nodes.statement: In $M$, $x \sqcap y = \bot$ iff $x_n \sqcap y_n = \bot$ at every block, and $x \le y^{\perp}$ iff $x_n \le (y_n)^{\perp}$ at every block (\texttt{ortho\_iff\_blockwise}). Both hold for arbitrary supports, not only for single-block elements.
nodes.section: 6.4 The descent ladder: MO$_2$ carried to infinity
nodes.label: lem:legs-localize

nodes.statement: Function extensionality and the pointwise product lemmas.
nodes.section: 6.4 The descent ladder: MO$_2$ carried to infinity

nodes.name: MO$_2$ caps orthogonal families at two
nodes.statement: No three nonzero elements of MO$_2$ are pairwise orthogonal; equivalently, any pairwise-orthogonal triple has a $\bot$ member (\texttt{mo2\_pairwise\_ortho\_one\_zero}).
nodes.section: 6.4 The descent ladder: MO$_2$ carried to infinity
nodes.label: lem:mo2-cap-two

nodes.statement: Finite case check over the six-element type.
nodes.section: 6.4 The descent ladder: MO$_2$ carried to infinity

nodes.name: The witness family is infinite and orthogonal
nodes.statement: For $n \ne m$, $a_n \le a_m^{\perp}$. The family is indexed by $\mathbb{N}$, so it is infinite.
nodes.section: 6.4 The descent ladder: MO$_2$ carried to infinity
nodes.label: lem:afam-ortho

nodes.statement: Blockwise by \ref{lem:legs-localize}. At block $k$ the only case that could fail is $k = n = m$, excluded by $n \ne m$; the rest are $a \le \top$, $\bot \le a^{\perp}$ and $\bot \le \top$. The supports $C_n = \{n\}$ are singletons, on which Navara's constancy clause is vacuous, so $p = \bigvee_n b|_{C_n}$ lands in the sublogic. General $\sigma$-orthocompleteness, for arbitrary $C$, is the cited result assumed at \ref{def:navara-l2}.
nodes.section: 6.4 The descent ladder: MO$_2$ carried to infinity

nodes.statement: A family $L \subseteq \mathcal{P}(\Omega)$ with $\emptyset, \Omega \in L$, closed under complement, and closed under countable \emph{disjoint} unions. nodes.label: thm:polish-cut-reduced

nodes.statement: \ref{thm:localization} splits a witness into (0) coherence, (i) empty kernel and (ii) no non-Dirac $\sigma$-state extending. If every $\sigma$-additive two-valued state is a point evaluation then clause (ii) holds vacuously, so being a witness is exactly (0) $\wedge$ (i), and "no witness" is exactly "coherent $\Rightarrow$ kernel nonempty".
nodes.section: 7.4 The OML gap --- the open question

nodes.name: Finite additivity is $\sigma$-additivity on a finite carrier
nodes.statement: On a finite $\Omega$ every finitely additive state satisfies the $\sigma$-condition on the whole carrier.
nodes.section: 7.4 The OML gap --- the open question
nodes.label: lem:finite-sigma

nodes.statement: A pairwise disjoint family in a finite space has only finitely many nonempty members --- choosing a point from each is injective --- so the countable union is the finite sup over that index set, and finite additivity applies to it.
nodes.section: 7.4 The OML gap --- the open question

nodes.name: $\Phi$ on finite carriers
nodes.statement: No finite $\sigma$-class admits a $\sigma$-essential witness; equivalently, a witness carrier is infinite. The finite and Boolean gates are independent: the four-point carrier of \ref{def:concrete-mo2} is finite and not intersection-closed.
nodes.section: 7.4 The OML gap --- the open question
nodes.label: thm:phi-finite

nodes.statement: Coherence supplies a finitely additive state extending the pattern; \ref{lem:finite-sigma} makes it $\sigma$-additive, so it is a global $\sigma$-additive two-valued state extending the pattern and the pattern is not $\sigma$-essential.
nodes.section: 7.4 The OML gap --- the open question

nodes.name: One block iff Boolean
nodes.statement: A carrier has a unique maximal block if and only if it is intersection-closed. Hence $\Phi$ holds on one-block carriers.
nodes.section: 7.4 The OML gap --- the open question
nodes.label: thm:one-block-iff-boolean

nodes.statement: If every pair is compatible the whole carrier is a compatible family, and maximality forces each maximal block to be all of it. Conversely each singleton $\{A\}$ extends to a maximal block, uniqueness puts $A$ and $B$ in the same one, and members of a block are compatible. The $\Phi$ half is then \ref{lem:boolean-no-witness}.
nodes.section: 7.4 The OML gap --- the open question

nodes.name: Concentration on a countable partition
nodes.statement: If the carrier contains a countable partition of $\Omega$, every $\sigma$-additive two-valued state is true on exactly one part.
nodes.section: 7.4 The OML gap --- the open question
nodes.label: lem:concentration-partition

nodes.statement: Existence is $\sigma$-additivity applied to the partition, whose union is $\Omega$; uniqueness is two-valuedness on a disjoint pair.
nodes.section: 7.4 The OML gap --- the open question

nodes.name: Countable carriers with singletons are point-determined
nodes.statement: If $\Omega$ is countable and every singleton lies in the carrier, then every $\sigma$-additive two-valued state agrees on the carrier with a point evaluation. Consequently a pattern there is a witness exactly when it is finitely coherent with empty kernel: clause (ii) of \ref{thm:localization} is vacuous, and the whole question is clause (i).
nodes.section: 7.4 The OML gap --- the open question
nodes.label: thm:countable-point-determined

nodes.statement: The singletons partition $\Omega$ into a countable pairwise disjoint family inside the carrier, so $\sigma$-additivity places the state's mass on one of them, at $\omega$ say; monotonicity and complement-additivity then give $s(A) = 1 \iff \omega \in A$ for every carrier set. For the consequence: any $\sigma$-additive state extending the pattern agrees with $\delta_\omega$ on the block, so $\delta_\omega$ extends it too and $\omega$ lies in the kernel.
nodes.section: 7.4 The OML gap --- the open question

nodes.name: The witness carrier is not a lattice
nodes.statement: $L_1$ has no meet at the cores: a greatest lower bound would have to be the slab $M \times \{0\}$, which is not in the carrier.
nodes.section: 7.4 The OML gap --- the open question
nodes.label: lem:witness-not-lattice

nodes.statement: Forced by the singletons, a greatest carrier lower bound of the cores would have to equal the slab $M \times \{0\}$ (\texttt{greatest\_lowerBound\_eq\_slab}). The slab is not in the carrier (\texttt{slab0\_not\_mem}): any normalized representation must give coordinate $0$ a code differing from the other three (\texttt{slab\_codes\_differ}, since the $f = 0$ trace is co-countable and the rest are countable), so the code is the odd-weight $1000$ or its complement $0111$, and \texttt{EvenCode} excludes both.
nodes.section: 7.4 The OML gap --- the open question

nodes.name: $L_1$ is not order-isomorphic to any $\sigma$-algebra
nodes.statement: There is no order isomorphism between the carrier of $L_1$ and the measurable sets of a $\sigma$-algebra, on any space.
nodes.section: 7.4 The OML gap --- the open question
nodes.label: cor:carrier-not-orderiso

nodes.statement: \texttt{MeetsExist} is a property of the carrier poset, so an order isomorphism transports it. The measurable sets of a $\sigma$-algebra are closed under intersection, so any two have a greatest measurable set below both; carrying that back along the isomorphism gives a greatest carrier element below any two carrier elements. \ref{lem:witness-not-lattice} says there is none below the two cores.
nodes.section: 7.4 The OML gap --- the open question

nodes.name: Central set
nodes.statement: $E$ lies in the carrier and $E \cap A$ is again in the carrier for every carrier element $A$.
nodes.section: 7.4 The OML gap --- the open question
nodes.label: def:central

nodes.name: All four traces of a central set agree
nodes.statement: A central $E$ has a single $\xi$ with $\mathrm{trace}(E,f) \approx \xi$ for every coordinate $f$.
nodes.section: 7.4 The OML gap --- the open question
nodes.label: thm:central-traces

nodes.statement: Coordinates $0,1,2$ carry countably equal traces, $\kappa_3$ is false, and even weight forces the fourth. Equal traces force equal codes, since $\kappa_a \neq \kappa_b$ would make $\xi \approx \xi^{c}$ and $M$ countable.
nodes.section: 7.4 The OML gap --- the open question

nodes.name: $\xi$-triviality, the paper's ${[E]} \in \{0,1\}$
nodes.statement: That common $\xi$ is countable or co-countable.
nodes.section: 7.4 The OML gap --- the open question
nodes.label: thm:xi-trivial

nodes.statement: Apply centrality at a core. $E \cap \mathrm{coreA}$ is again a carrier element, so \ref{thm:normal-form} represents it as $\eta^{(\kappa)}$ with $\kappa_3$ false. Meeting $\mathrm{coreA}$ empties coordinate $3$, where the normal form is anchored: $\emptyset \approx \eta$, so $\eta$ is countable. Coordinate $0$ is untouched by the meet and carries $\xi$, so $\xi \approx \eta$ or $\xi \approx \eta^{c}$ --- countable or co-countable respectively.
nodes.section: 7.4 The OML gap --- the open question

nodes.name: The centre is trivial modulo the countable ideal
nodes.statement: A central set is countable or co-countable.
nodes.section: 7.4 The OML gap --- the open question
nodes.label: cor:centre

nodes.statement: \ref{thm:central-traces} reduces the question to $\xi$ and \ref{thm:xi-trivial} makes $\xi$ trivial; countable traces force a countable set and co-countable traces a co-countable one.
nodes.section: 7.4 The OML gap --- the open question

nodes.name: Segregated carrier, and non-segregation
nodes.statement: A carrier is \emph{segregated} when every finitely additive state is blockwise pointed --- each maximal block supplies a kernel point. \emph{Non-segregated} is the negation.
nodes.section: 7.4 The OML gap --- the open question
nodes.label: def:segregated

nodes.name: Non-segregation is forced by the witness
nodes.statement: A witness carrier is non-segregated.
nodes.section: 7.4 The OML gap --- the open question
nodes.label: lem:witness-nonsegregated

nodes.statement: On a segregated carrier blockwise $\sigma$-additivity globalises, so every finitely additive state is $\sigma$-additive; a finitely coherent pattern then has a $\sigma$-additive realization and is not $\sigma$-essential.
nodes.section: 7.4 The OML gap --- the open question

nodes.name: The centre, and essential irreducibility
nodes.statement: $E$ is \emph{central} when it lies in the carrier and $E \cap A$ does too for every carrier element $A$. The carrier is \emph{essentially irreducible} when every central element is countable or co-countable.
nodes.section: 7.4 The OML gap --- the open question
nodes.label: def:essentially-irreducible

nodes.name: The admissible carrier class
nodes.statement: Essentially irreducible and non-segregated.
nodes.section: 7.4 The OML gap --- the open question
nodes.label: def:admissible

nodes.name: The witness carrier is admissible
nodes.statement: $L_1$ is essentially irreducible and non-segregated. So the sharp Exit-A target --- a witness on an admissible carrier --- is inhabited in ZFC by the $\omega_1$ product-Ulam witness.
nodes.section: 7.4 The OML gap --- the open question
nodes.label: thm:l1-admissible

nodes.statement: Essential irreducibility is \ref{cor:centre}: every central element of $L_1$ is countable or co-countable. Non-segregation is \ref{lem:witness-nonsegregated} applied to the witness of \ref{thm:psi-zfc}.
nodes.section: 7.4 The OML gap --- the open question

nodes.name: Irreducibility proper
nodes.statement: The centre is trivial: every central element is $\emptyset$ or $\Omega$. Strictly stronger than \ref{def:essentially-irreducible}.
nodes.section: 7.4 The OML gap --- the open question
nodes.label: def:irreducible

nodes.name: The concrete descent carrier is reducible
nodes.statement: Every block of \ref{def:concrete-descent} is central, so the centre has one element per subset of $\mathbb{N}$ and the carrier is not irreducible. It satisfies \ref{def:essentially-irreducible} vacuously, the carrier being countable; $L_1$'s carrier is uncountable, so there the dichotomy is real.
nodes.section: 7.4 The OML gap --- the open question
nodes.label: thm:descent-not-irreducible

nodes.statement: Meeting a carrier element with a whole block leaves each fibre either that fibre or empty, both in the four-point carrier, so blocks are central. Block $0$ is neither empty nor everything. Vacuity of the essential form is countability of $\mathbb{N} \times \{0,1\}^{2}$.
nodes.section: 7.4 The OML gap --- the open question

nodes.name: $\Psi_{\mathrm{OML}}$ --- the lattice form
nodes.statement: The same existence sentence with latticehood (\texttt{MeetsExist}) adjoined to the carrier.
nodes.section: 7.4 The OML gap --- the open question
nodes.label: def:psi-oml

nodes.name: $\Phi$
nodes.statement: $\Phi$: does every concrete, $\sigma$-complete, non-Boolean, essentially irreducible OML have each finite trace of each finitely additive two-valued state reproduced by some $\sigma$-additive one? A positive answer is the negation of $\Psi_{\mathrm{OML}}$. Open.
nodes.section: 7.4 The OML gap --- the open question
nodes.label: rmk:phi-open

nodes.name: Countably compact class
nodes.statement: A family $\mathcal{K}$ of sets such that every sequence from $\mathcal{K}$ with the finite intersection property has nonempty total intersection.
nodes.section: 7.5 Inner regularity: what forces $\sigma$-additivity, and what refuses it
nodes.label: def:countably-compact-class

nodes.name: Marczewski approximation, two-valued in-block form
nodes.statement: Every value-$1$ member $E$ of the family carries a value-$1$ inner witness sandwiched below a class member: $D \subseteq K \subseteq E$ with $K \in \mathcal{K}$.
nodes.section: 7.5 Inner regularity: what forces $\sigma$-additivity, and what refuses it
nodes.label: def:approximates-on

nodes.name: Compact transport
nodes.statement: On a carrier where meets exist, a finitely additive two-valued state approximated on every maximal block by a countably compact class satisfies the $\sigma$-condition on the whole carrier.
nodes.section: 7.5 Inner regularity: what forces $\sigma$-additivity, and what refuses it
nodes.label: thm:compact-transport

nodes.statement: Run inside one maximal block and glue. Tails of a disjoint sequence are value-$1$, so their inner witnesses have value-$1$ --- hence nonempty --- finite intersections; the sandwiching compacts therefore have the finite intersection property, and countable compactness contradicts the empty tail intersection. Marczewski 1953, 4(i), two-valued.
nodes.section: 7.5 Inner regularity: what forces $\sigma$-additivity, and what refuses it

nodes.name: A field of sets and a two-valued state on it
nodes.statement: A field of sets: finite closure only, no $\sigma$-structure.
nodes.section: 7.5 Inner regularity: what forces $\sigma$-additivity, and what refuses it
nodes.label: def:set-field

nodes.name: Inner regularity (8.1)
nodes.statement: Every value-$1$ member of the field contains a value-$1$ in-field \emph{compact}.
nodes.section: 7.5 Inner regularity: what forces $\sigma$-additivity, and what refuses it
nodes.label: def:inner-regular-81

nodes.name: Theorem-let R: (8.1) forces Dirac
nodes.statement: On a Hausdorff space, a two-valued finitely additive state satisfying (8.1) has nonempty $\mathcal{K}_1$ (its value-$1$ in-field compacts), nonempty $D = \bigcap \mathcal{K}_1$, and \emph{equals} $\delta_\omega$ on the field for every $\omega \in D$.
nodes.section: 7.5 Inner regularity: what forces $\sigma$-additivity, and what refuses it
nodes.label: thm:dirac-forcing

nodes.statement: Value-$1$ in-field compacts are $\cap$-stable (compact $\cap$ closed, and Hausdorff makes compacts closed), finite intersections are value-$1$ hence nonempty, and compactness of one fixed member turns an empty total intersection into an empty finite one.
nodes.section: 7.5 Inner regularity: what forces $\sigma$-additivity, and what refuses it

nodes.name: The co-countable state
nodes.statement: On an uncountable $\Omega$, the countable/co-countable $\sigma$-field with the state that is $1$ exactly on the co-countable sets.
nodes.section: 7.5 Inner regularity: what forces $\sigma$-additivity, and what refuses it
nodes.label: def:cocountable-state

nodes.name: It is not Dirac
nodes.statement: For every $\omega$ there is a carrier set of value $1$ missing $\omega$ --- namely $\{\omega\}^{c}$.
nodes.section: 7.5 Inner regularity: what forces $\sigma$-additivity, and what refuses it
nodes.label: lem:cocountable-not-dirac

nodes.statement: A singleton is countable, so its complement is co-countable and carries value $1$.
nodes.section: 7.5 Inner regularity: what forces $\sigma$-additivity, and what refuses it

nodes.name: Theorem-let P: (8.1) fails, at a named set
nodes.statement: On an uncountable second-countable Hausdorff space, (8.1) fails at the specific set $F = X \setminus \{x\}$ for $x$ a condensation point.
nodes.section: 7.5 Inner regularity: what forces $\sigma$-additivity, and what refuses it
nodes.label: thm:cocountable-fails-81

nodes.statement: Via \texttt{exists\_condensation\_point}: at $x$ no open neighbourhood is countable, which is all that is consumed.
nodes.section: 7.5 Inner regularity: what forces $\sigma$-additivity, and what refuses it

nodes.name: The all-Hausdorff strengthening
nodes.statement: On \emph{any} uncountable Hausdorff space the co-countable state fails (8.1) somewhere --- no second countability needed.
nodes.section: 7.5 Inner regularity: what forces $\sigma$-additivity, and what refuses it
nodes.label: cor:cocountable-fails-hausdorff

nodes.statement: By \ref{thm:dirac-forcing}, (8.1) would make the state a Dirac restriction, and \ref{lem:cocountable-not-dirac} says it is none.
nodes.section: 7.5 Inner regularity: what forces $\sigma$-additivity, and what refuses it

nodes.name: The cofinite topology is not Hausdorff
nodes.statement: On the cofinite topology over an infinite set, with the finite/cofinite field and the cofinite state, every set is compact and (8.1) holds, yet the state is not Dirac. By \ref{thm:dirac-forcing} the space is not Hausdorff.
nodes.section: 7.5 Inner regularity: what forces $\sigma$-additivity, and what refuses it
nodes.label: prop:cofinite-red-flag

nodes.statement: Run \ref{thm:dirac-forcing} on the cofinite data; the conclusion fails, so its Hausdorff hypothesis does.
nodes.section: 7.5 Inner regularity: what forces $\sigma$-additivity, and what refuses it

nodes.name: Layer-injective simple cycle
nodes.statement: For $L \geq 1$ the \emph{layered ring} $R_L(\rho)$ has vertex set $\mathbb{Z}_L \times A$ and arcs $(i,a) \to (i+1 \bmod L, b)$ for every $(a,b) \in \rho$. A simple cycle of \emph{winding} $k$ is a closed walk of length $kL$ with all vertices distinct. $\mathrm{LISC}_k(L)$ holds when one exists. Encoded by the state sequence $W$ on positions $t < kL$: $\rho$-steps between consecutive positions, a closing $\rho$-step, and the simplicity clause --- same layer $(t \bmod L)$ plus same state implies same position.
nodes.section: 8.1 The two sides: cycles in the layered ring, walks in the tuple digraph
nodes.label: def:lisc

nodes.name: Tuple digraph and rotation walks
nodes.statement: $T_k(\rho)$ has as vertices the \emph{injective} $k$-tuples $u \in A^k$, with arcs $u \to v$ iff $(u_j, v_j) \in \rho$ for every $j$. For $r \in \mathbb{Z}_k$ let $\sigma_r(u)_j = u_{j+r}$. Then $\mathrm{TR}_k^{(r)}(L)$ holds when some length-$L$ walk in $T_k(\rho)$ runs from a $u$ to $\sigma_r(u)$. Encoded as $\tau : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{Z}_k \to A$ with $\tau_i$ injective for $i \leq L$, coordinatewise $\rho$-arcs, and endpoint $\tau_L\,j = \tau_0\,(j+r)$.
nodes.section: 8.1 The two sides: cycles in the layered ring, walks in the tuple digraph
nodes.label: def:tr

nodes.name: Step 2: extraction
nodes.statement: For $0 < L$, $\mathrm{LISC}_k(L)$ implies $\mathrm{TR}_k^{(1)}(L)$.
nodes.section: 8.2 Theorem P
nodes.label: lem:extraction

nodes.statement: Read the $k$ strands at each layer: set $\tau_i[j]$ to the state of $W[jL+i]$. Injectivity of each $\tau_i$ is forced by simplicity: distinct vertices at the same layer have distinct states. The endpoint computes to $\sigma_1(\tau_0)$.
nodes.section: 8.2 Theorem P

nodes.name: Step 3: assembly
nodes.statement: For $0 < L$, $\mathrm{TR}_k^{(1)}(L)$ implies $\mathrm{LISC}_k(L)$.
nodes.section: 8.2 Theorem P
nodes.label: lem:assembly

nodes.statement: Place position $t = jL+i$ at vertex $(i, \tau_i[j])$. Arcs within a strand are the tuple-walk arcs; at a strand boundary the rotation endpoint supplies $\tau_L[j] = \tau_0[j+1]$, which is the state at position $(j+1)L$, and at $j = k-1$ this is the closure. Simplicity follows from the layer clock plus injectivity of each $\tau_i$.
nodes.section: 8.2 Theorem P

nodes.name: Step 4: generator conjugation
nodes.statement: If $r$ is a unit of $\mathbb{Z}_k$, that is $\gcd(r,k)=1$, then $\mathrm{TR}_k^{(r)}(L)$ holds iff $\mathrm{TR}_k^{(1)}(L)$ does.
nodes.section: 8.2 Theorem P
nodes.label: lem:conjugation

nodes.statement: The slot relabelling $P(u)[j] = u[j\bar r]$, with $\bar r = r^{-1}$, is a bijection of injective tuples, preserves arcs (a fixed coordinate permutation), and conjugates the rotations via $(j+r)\bar r = j\bar r + 1$.
nodes.section: 8.2 Theorem P

nodes.name: Theorem P: pruning, phase-parametrized
nodes.statement: For every $\rho$, every $L \geq 1$, every $k \geq 1$ and every $r$ generating $\mathbb{Z}_k$, $\mathrm{LISC}_k(L)$ holds iff $\mathrm{TR}_k^{(r)}(L)$ does.
nodes.section: 8.2 Theorem P
nodes.label: thm:pruning

nodes.statement: Conjugate to $r=1$ by \ref{lem:conjugation}, then combine \ref{lem:extraction} and \ref{lem:assembly}.
nodes.section: 8.2 Theorem P

nodes.name: Lemma NG: assembly half
nodes.statement: Suppose the rotation $r$ closes an orbit of size $m$, witnessed by an injective slot map $f : \mathbb{Z}_m \to \mathbb{Z}_k$ with $f(j+1) = f(j) + r$. Then a rotation-$r$ tuple walk certifies $\mathrm{LISC}_m(L)$: winding $m$, not winding $k$. For a generator $m = k$; for $\gcd(r,k) = d > 1$ it is the strictly weaker $m = k/d$.
nodes.section: 8.2 Theorem P
nodes.label: lem:ng

nodes.statement: Read the walk through $f$: this is a rotation-$1$ witness of width $m$, so \ref{lem:assembly} assembles it. The instance $m=k$, $f = \mathrm{id}$, $r=1$ recovers Step 3. Not formalized: that the $d$ orbit cycles are pairwise vertex-disjoint.
nodes.section: 8.2 Theorem P

nodes.name: Eventually periodic subset of the naturals
nodes.statement: $S \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ is eventually periodic when there are a threshold $s$ and a period $p > 0$ with $L \in S$ iff $L+p \in S$, for every $L \geq s$. Finite unions, intersections and complements are again eventually periodic, with threshold $\max$ and period $\mathrm{lcm}$.
nodes.section: 8.3 Theorem B
nodes.label: def:evperiodic

nodes.name: The k-cap
nodes.statement: If $0 < L$ and $\mathrm{LISC}_k(L)$ then $k \leq |A|$.
nodes.section: 8.3 Theorem B
nodes.label: lem:kcap

nodes.statement: The positions $0, L, \dots, (k-1)L$ all sit at layer $0$ and are pairwise distinct, so their states are $k$ distinct elements of $A$. Pigeonhole.
nodes.section: 8.3 Theorem B

nodes.name: Unsafe and Safe
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{Unsafe}(\rho)$ is the set of $L \geq 1$ with $\mathrm{LISC}_k(L)$ for some $k \geq 2$, and $\mathrm{Safe}(\rho)$ is its complement among the positives. Ring reconstruction $C_L = R_L$ holds exactly on $\mathrm{Safe}(\rho)$.
nodes.section: 8.3 Theorem B
nodes.label: def:unsafe-safe

nodes.name: Unsafe is a finite union of reachability sets
nodes.statement: For finite $A$, $\mathrm{Unsafe}(\rho)$ is the union of $\mathrm{TR}_k^{(1)}$ over $2 \leq k \leq |A|$.
nodes.section: 8.3 Theorem B
nodes.label: lem:unsafe-biunion

nodes.statement: The k-cap bounds the winding by $|A|$, making the union finite; Theorem P converts each $\mathrm{LISC}_k$ into $\mathrm{TR}_k^{(1)}$.
nodes.section: 8.3 Theorem B

nodes.name: Deterministic orbits in a finite type are eventually periodic
nodes.statement: For $f : \beta \to \beta$ with $\beta$ finite and any $b$, there are $s$ and $p > 0$ with $f^{n+p}(b) = f^{n}(b)$ for all $n \geq s$.
nodes.section: 8.3 Theorem B
nodes.label: lem:iterate

nodes.statement: The sequence $n \mapsto f^n(b)$ cannot be injective, so it repeats; being generated deterministically, it is periodic from the first repeat onward.
nodes.section: 8.3 Theorem B

nodes.name: Reachability is an iterate, and matches the raw walk
nodes.statement: Length-$n$ reachability in $T_k(\rho)$ is the $n$-th iterate of a single step operator on relations over injective tuples, and it holds between $u$ and $v$ exactly when a raw tuple walk of the shape in \ref{def:tr} runs from $u$ to $v$.
nodes.section: 8.3 Theorem B
nodes.label: lem:reach-walk

nodes.statement: Induction on $n$, rebuilding the walk one layer at a time.
nodes.section: 8.3 Theorem B

nodes.name: Per-k eventual periodicity
nodes.statement: For finite $A$, the set of $L$ with $\mathrm{TR}_k^{(1)}(L)$ is eventually periodic.
nodes.section: 8.3 Theorem B
nodes.label: lem:evper-tr

nodes.statement: The vertex set of $T_k(\rho)$ is finite, hence so is the type of relations on it; apply \ref{lem:iterate} to the step operator and transport along \ref{lem:reach-walk}.
nodes.section: 8.3 Theorem B

nodes.name: Theorem B
nodes.statement: For every relation $\rho$ on a finite alphabet, $\mathrm{Safe}(\rho)$ is eventually periodic: there are a threshold $S$ and a period $P > 0$ with $L \in \mathrm{Safe}(\rho)$ iff $L+P \in \mathrm{Safe}(\rho)$, for every $L \geq S$. Membership is therefore decided by a finite table.
nodes.section: 8.3 Theorem B
nodes.label: thm:B

nodes.statement: $\mathrm{Unsafe}$ is a finite union of eventually periodic sets by \ref{lem:unsafe-biunion} and \ref{lem:evper-tr}, hence eventually periodic with threshold the max of the thresholds and period the lcm of the periods; $\mathrm{Safe}$ is its complement among the positives.
nodes.section: 8.3 Theorem B

nodes.name: Lemma NG, orbit-map half
nodes.statement: A rotation-$r$ tuple walk certifies a simple cycle of winding $\mathrm{addOrderOf}(r) = k/\gcd(r,k)$, equal to $k$ exactly when $r$ generates.
nodes.section: 8.4 Lemma NG
nodes.label: lem:ng-orbit

nodes.statement: The orbit map is \texttt{ZMod.lift} applied to \texttt{zmultiplesHom}, so $f(j+1) = f(j) + r$ follows from \texttt{map\_add}; injectivity is a divisibility step. Feeding this to \ref{lem:ng} gives the winding-$m$ conclusion. Still open: pairwise disjointness of the $d$ orbit cycles.
nodes.section: 8.4 Lemma NG

nodes.name: Lemma NG, refutation half
nodes.statement: For the directed 4-cycle at $L = 2$ and the non-generator $r = 2$ ($\gcd(2,4) = 2$): $\mathrm{TR}_4^{(2)}(2)$ holds, $\mathrm{LISC}_2(2)$ holds, and $\mathrm{LISC}_4(2)$ \emph{fails}.
nodes.section: 8.4 Lemma NG
nodes.label: thm:ng-refute

nodes.statement: The relation is a function, so every vertex of the layered ring has out-degree one and a walk is determined by its start; it returns to its starting state after four steps. A winding-4 simple cycle needs eight pairwise distinct positions, but positions $0$ and $4$ share a layer and a state. The winding-2 cycle and the rotation-2 slot walk $\tau_i(j) = j + i$ are exhibited directly. So a rotation witness at a non-generator certifies winding $k/d = 2$, not winding $k$.
nodes.section: 8.4 Lemma NG

nodes.name: The subshift of a relation
nodes.statement: $\Sigma_{\rho} = \{\omega : \mathbb{Z} \to A \mid \rho(\omega_{t+1}, \omega_t) \text{ for all } t\}$, the bi-infinite $\rho$-trajectories inside the sensor streams.
nodes.section: 8.5 Relational delay systems: the pruning objects as delay data
nodes.label: def:subshift

nodes.name: The trajectory of a cycle
nodes.statement: From a cycle witness $W$ and modulus $n$, the stream carrying $W$ at index $(-t) \bmod n$. It is $n$-periodic (\texttt{cycleStream\_periodic}).
nodes.section: 8.5 Relational delay systems: the pruning objects as delay data
nodes.label: def:cycle-stream

nodes.name: A cycle is a trajectory
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{cycleStream}\,W\,(kL) \in \Sigma_{\rho}$.
nodes.section: 8.5 Relational delay systems: the pruning objects as delay data
nodes.label: lem:cycle-stream-subshift

nodes.statement: Interior positions are the cycle's own arcs; where the index rolls over the condition is the closing arc $\rho(W_{kL-1}, W_0)$.
nodes.section: 8.5 Relational delay systems: the pruning objects as delay data

nodes.name: Layer-injectivity is delay-injectivity
nodes.statement: If $\mathrm{LISC}_k(L)$ then there is a $\rho$-trajectory $\omega$, periodic of period $kL$, whose depth-$k$, lag-$L$ delay query is injective.
nodes.section: 8.5 Relational delay systems: the pruning objects as delay data
nodes.label: thm:lisc-delay-witness

nodes.statement: Take $\omega = \mathrm{cycleStream}\,W\,(kL)$; \ref{lem:cycle-stream-subshift} gives membership, and periodicity is immediate. The delay query at lag $L$ and depth $k$ samples $\omega$ at $0, -L, \dots, -(k-1)L$, which are the positions $0, L, \dots, (k-1)L$ of the cycle --- the $k$ positions sharing layer $0$. By \ref{def:lisc}'s simplicity clause these carry distinct states.

nodes.name: $\mathrm{Unsafe}$, in the delay vocabulary

nodes.statement: The complete relation on $\{\bot,\top\}$ satisfies $\mathrm{LISC}_2(1)$, so the conclusion of \ref{thm:lisc-delay-witness} is inhabited.

nodes.name: The two halves of a deterministic trajectory
nodes.statement: For $\omega \in \Sigma_{\mathrm{graph}(T)}$: the non-positive half is the forward orbit of the base point, $\omega(-n) = T^n(\omega_0)$; the positive half is a coherent backward orbit, $T^n(\omega_n) = \omega_0$.

nodes.statement: Induction in each direction, from the trajectory condition read forwards and backwards respectively.

nodes.name: Deterministic is a subclass
nodes.statement: For $\omega \in \Sigma_{\mathrm{graph}(T)}$ and an observable $h$, the delay data the relational picture assigns to $\omega$ equals the delay data the deterministic picture assigns to $\omega_0$.
nodes.section: 8.5 Relational delay systems: the pruning objects as delay data
nodes.label: thm:deterministic-subclass

nodes.statement: Both sides evaluate at $-(k\tau)$, which \ref{lem:graph-subshift-halves} makes $T^{k\tau}(\omega_0)$.

nodes.name: Base points outside the subshift
nodes.statement: Being the base of a bi-infinite trajectory forces $\omega_0 \in \mathrm{range}(T^n)$ for every $n$. For non-surjective $T$ there are therefore points based at no relational trajectory whose delay data is still defined by \ref{def:orbit-stream}.
